our road is gone under a big pile of dirt and rocks w trees mixed in, is it ok to walk over it to get to my moms or shud we wait for help

Do not walk over the pile. It can shift and crush you.
1. Stay off the dirt, rocks, and trees. Landslide debris is unstable and can move again.
2. Move away from the base of the slope and uphill if you can. More slides can follow.
3. Call 911. Tell them the road is blocked and where you are.
4. Wait for help to clear it. Do not try to cross to reach your mom.
5. If you can reach her safely by phone, call and tell her you are safe and waiting.

fingers are white and hard and i cant feel em no more what do i do

Get out of the cold now. Frostbite is happening.
1. Move indoors or into a warm place. Stop the cold exposure first.
2. Do not rub the fingers or use snow. Rubbing damages the skin.
3. Warm fingers in warm water about 100-105F (37-40C) for 20-30 minutes. Not hot water, not a fire, not a heater.
4. Do not pop blisters. Loosely wrap fingers in clean cloth.
5. Call 911 if fingers stay white, hard, or turn black, or if the person is confused or very cold. Get medical help for frostbite.

water pullin back is it coming now

Move to high ground or inland right now. Do not wait.
1. Leave the beach and shore immediately. Water pulling back means a wave may hit in minutes.
2. Go on foot if you can. Roads may jam.
3. Get as high up or as far inland as you can. Upper floors of a strong building also help if you cannot leave.
4. Do not go back to watch or help until officials say it is safe. Later waves can be bigger.
5. Call 911 if someone is trapped or hurt.

walkin outside dark w my mom shes shakin bad n slow what do i do

Get her inside a warm place now.
1. Call 911. Bad shaking and slow movement can be a medical emergency.
2. Get her out of the cold and wind. Remove any wet clothes.
3. Warm her slowly with blankets and your body heat. Do not use hot water, a hot bath, or rub her skin — that can harm her.
4. Do not give alcohol or caffeine. If she is awake and can swallow, give warm sweet drinks.
5. Keep her lying still and watch her breathing until help comes.

mall 2nd floor someone hurt bad phone dyin wat do we do

Call 911 now. A badly hurt person needs help fast.
1. Keep your phone on and save battery. Turn down brightness, stop apps. You may need it to reach rescuers.
2. Shout for mall staff or security. They know exits and can bring help.
3. Do not move the hurt person unless there is fire, smoke, or falling debris right there. Moving them can make injuries worse.
4. If there is smoke or fire, get low and leave by the nearest stairs. Do not use elevators.
5. Stay with the hurt person and keep talking to them until help comes.

train soud getting louder out window shuld i open it or no

Do not open the window. Get away from it now.
1. Move to a basement, or a small interior room with no windows on the lowest floor. A loud roaring train sound can mean a tornado is coming.
2. Stay away from windows and outside walls. Flying glass and debris cause most injuries.
3. Cover your head and neck with your arms, a helmet, or blankets. Protect yourself from falling debris.
4. Keep your phone and shoes with you. You may need to leave fast after it passes.
Opening a window is not safe. It does not protect the house and puts you near glass.

im in my apt alone n cut my arm bad, can i still tape up the door n window before i deal w it

Stop the bleeding first. Your cut can kill you faster than anything outside.
1. Press hard on the cut with a clean cloth or towel and hold it. Keep pressing without lifting to check.
2. Call 911 now. Say you are alone and bleeding badly.
3. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top. Do not remove the first cloth.
4. Raise the arm above your heart if you can, and keep pressing.
5. Only after bleeding is controlled, tape the door and window shut. Close and seal them fast, then stay inside.
Do not tape over the wound or use a tourniquet unless bleeding will not stop with hard pressure.

fridge starts warmin, can i put milk on porch? its 30 outside n power goin on 12 hrs

Keep the fridge door closed as much as possible. A closed fridge keeps food cold about 4 hours.
1. Put the milk on the porch only if it is 40°F (4°C) or colder outside and out of the sun. Cold air slows bacteria.
2. Keep it in a closed container or bag. Animals and pests can get into open food.
3. Do not refreeze or keep milk that sat above 40°F for over 2 hours. It can make you sick.
4. When power returns, throw out milk that smells or looks off. Do not taste-test it.

hail big as golf balls hitting us

Get inside a sturdy building right now.
1. Stay away from windows and skylights. Hail and wind can shatter glass.
2. If you are in a car, stay in it with windows up. A car is safer than open ground.
3. Do not shelter under trees. Lightning and falling branches are a risk.
4. Wait until the hail stops before going back out.
If someone is badly hurt, call 911.

WATER IS AT MY WAIST in the livingroom, attic has no window, what do i do

Do not go into the windowless attic. It can trap you.
1. Water at your waist will keep rising, so get higher, but to a floor or room with a window you can escape or signal from.
2. Go to the highest floor that has a window. Open it, or be ready to break it, to reach the roof or call for help.
3. Keep clear of outlets and wires in the water.
4. Call 911 now. Say water is waist high and rising, give your address, and wave from the window to signal.

roof of gynasium is rattling bad, im in the hallway alone is it safer under the bleachers or in the bathroom?

Get out from under that rattling roof now.
1. Move to the bathroom if it has no windows. A small inner room is safer than a big roof span.
2. Do not go under the bleachers. They are still under the rattling roof and can collapse or be hit by debris.
3. Sit on the floor, away from windows and mirrors, and cover your head with your arms.
4. If the roof starts to fall or you hear cracking, drop low and protect your head.
5. Call 911 if anyone is hurt or the building is failing.

is the hose water safe to fill buckets after all that dry spell

Don't drink water from a garden hose.
1. Use hose water only for flushing toilets or washing, not drinking or cooking. Hoses and standing water can carry germs and lead.
2. For drinking, use bottled water or water you can boil for 1 minute.
3. If your tap water is running, fill buckets from the indoor tap instead. It is safer than a hose.
4. Check with your local water utility for any boil-water notice before drinking tap water.

rooftop water rising quick friend cant swim its dark what do we do

Stay as high as you safely can and keep back from the edge.
1. Move to the highest solid point on the roof, away from the water. Rising water can pull you off.
2. Keep your friend away from the edge and hold onto something solid. They cannot swim, so falling in is deadly.
3. Call 911 now and say you are on a roof, water rising, one person cannot swim. Stay on the line.
4. Signal for rescue: turn on phone flashlight or wave a light. Rescuers need to see you in the dark.
5. Do not go into the water to swim or wade. Only use floating items if water is already at you.
Do not enter the water. It is not safe.

candle fell over n curtain smoking but lights still out, should we just pour water n stay put?

Do not pour water on a smoking curtain. It can spread fire or burn you.
1. Blow out or smother the candle safely. Remove the heat source first.
2. If the curtain is only smoking and no flames: unplug nearby cords, move people away from the smoke, and open a window only if it is safe and smoke is not being drawn in.
3. If you see flames or the smoke is growing: get everyone outside now and call 911. Do not stay put.
4. If smoke is filling the room: get low and leave. Smoke is more dangerous than the dark.
5. Call 911 if there is any fire, smoke spreading, or someone is hurt.

city said restrictions start monday n the lawn is already crunching under my feet, should i fill the bathtubs now or wait

Start storing water safely now, but don't panic-fill every tub.
1. Fill clean containers first. Sealed bottles and food-grade jugs stay safe longer than an open tub.
2. If you fill the bathtub, clean it and cover it. An open tub collects dirt and germs.
3. Keep at least 1 gallon per person per day. That covers drinking and basic hygiene.
4. Follow the city's restriction rules. Storing water is fine; wasting it is not.
5. Call 911 only if someone is in danger now.

waves hittin our apartment bldg my freind cant walk wat do i do

Move to the highest floor you can reach now.
1. Help your friend up stairs — carry or support them. Water rises fast; high ground saves lives.
2. Do not go outside or down to the street. Moving water can knock you down and drown you.
3. Stay away from windows and outside walls. Waves can break glass.
4. Call 911 when safe. Say your friend cannot walk.
5. If water reaches your floor, go higher. Do not use elevators.

radiation alert on my phone, wind is blowing toward my house, do i shut all the windows and stay put or should we go now

Get inside your house now and close all windows and doors.
1. Turn off the heating, air conditioning, and any fans. These pull outside air and particles into your home.
2. Go to an interior room with few windows and stay there. Walls and distance reduce radiation exposure.
3. Do not go outside or drive away unless officials tell you to evacuate. Leaving during a plume can expose you to more radiation.
4. Keep your phone on and listen for official alerts. Follow their instructions on evacuation or staying put.
5. Call 911 only if someone is in immediate danger.

should we still drink tap water its coming out brown n cloudy

Do not drink the tap water right now. Brown, cloudy water can carry germs or chemicals.
1. Use bottled or stored water for drinking and cooking. If you have none, let the water sit and see if the brown settles — but still don't drink it unless officials say it's safe.
2. Do not use it to make baby formula, brush teeth, or wash wounds.
3. Boiling kills germs but does NOT remove chemicals — so boiling is not enough here.
4. Call 911 if anyone has bad stomach pain, vomiting, or trouble breathing.
5. Check with your local water utility or emergency alerts for a boil-water notice.

smell gas by the stove, shut valve off or get ouy?

Get everyone out now. Do not touch light switches or use your phone inside.
1. Leave the door open as you go. Fresh air and an escape route matter more than the stove.
2. Shut the gas valve only if it is right beside you and you can turn it by hand. Then keep leaving.
3. Do not light anything, smoke, or plug or unplug anything. A spark can ignite the gas.
4. From outside, call 911. Tell them you smell gas.

my kids got runs since the water came back, should i be worred

Stop giving your kids tap water for now. Use bottled or boiled water until officials say it is safe.
1. Give safe water often in small sips. Diarrhea loses water fast; kids dehydrate quickly.
2. Watch for danger signs: no pee, dry mouth, sunken eyes, sleepiness, or blood in stool. Call 911 if you see these.
3. Wash hands with safe water and soap after diapers or toilet. Germs spread easily.
4. If diarrhea is bad or lasts more than a day, get medical help. Don't wait.
Tap water that looks clear can still have germs. Boiling for 1 minute kills them.

shud we cancel trip next week?

Don't travel unless it is essential. Staying home is the safer choice.
1. Check official local rules for your area and destination. Rules can change fast and affect whether travel is allowed.
2. If anyone is sick or exposed, stay home and isolate. Travel can spread illness to others.
3. If you must go, avoid crowds, wash hands often, and wear a mask in public. These lower your risk.
4. Call 911 if anyone has severe trouble breathing or is in danger.
What kind of danger are you worried about?

legs gave out cant carry him n phone at 2% wats closst cold place

Call 911 now. Someone who can't stand needs emergency help.
1. Put him in shade or the coolest spot you can reach. Don't drag or carry him far — that can hurt him.
2. Cool him fast: wet cloth or water on skin, fan him, loosen tight clothes. Fast cooling saves lives in heat.
3. Give small sips of water only if he is awake and can swallow. No water if he is confused or unconscious.
4. Stay with him and keep the phone on to save battery. Call 911 again if he gets worse.

wall of water coming down my street can i get to the 3rd floor before it hits

Go up to the 3rd floor right now, as high as you can.
1. Move fast and take nothing with you. Seconds matter; the water can be faster than you.
2. Use stairs, never an elevator. Power may fail and trap you.
3. If the building is close and solid, get inside and climb. If the water is already at the door, go to the highest floor you can reach.
4. Stay high and away from windows. The wave can break glass and pull you out.
5. Do not go outside or downhill to watch or flee. Call 911 if you can, but only after you are up high.

is it ok to still go church sunday

Stay home and join church online or by phone this Sunday.
1. Avoid crowded indoor gatherings. Close contact spreads illness fast.
2. Check if your church offers livestream or call-in. Many do.
3. If you must go out, keep distance from others and wear a mask. This lowers risk.
4. Follow your local health rules. They may limit gatherings.
5. Call 911 if someone has trouble breathing or is in danger.

im walkin outside alone n see the ocean draggin way out can i still make it uphill

Go uphill and inland right now. Do not go near the water.
1. Move fast to high ground or far inland. The ocean pulling back means a tsunami may come soon.
2. Drop anything heavy that slows you. Seconds matter.
3. Stay away from the beach, harbor, and river mouths. Waves can rush up them.
4. Keep going until you are well above the shoreline or far inland. Do not stop to watch.
5. Call 911 only if someone is trapped or hurt. Stay on high ground until officials say it is safe.

is it ok to send my kid to school if there was a case in his class last wk

Check your child for symptoms first.
1. If your child has fever, cough, sore throat, or feels sick, keep them home and call your doctor. Going to school can spread illness.
2. If they have no symptoms, check what the school and local health department told you to do. Follow that advice.
3. If your child was a close contact, follow the health department's quarantine or testing instructions.
4. Watch for symptoms for the next several days. If they get sick, keep them home.
Call 911 only if breathing is hard or they are very ill.

water bursting thru the parking lot is it ok to drive thru

Do not drive through it. Turn around now.
1. Move away from the water and get to high ground on foot. Moving water can hide a collapsed road or wash a car away.
2. Do not walk or drive into or near the water. The ground under it may be hollow or giving way.
3. Keep others back and away from the edge.
4. Call 911. Say water is bursting through a parking lot and people may be in danger.
5. If water is rising fast around you, go up — upstairs or higher ground — and stay out of basements and low spots.

hail punched holes in my roof shingles will ceiling give out?

Get out from under the damaged ceiling now. A wet ceiling can sag and fall.
1. Move to a lower floor or a room with no damage. Stay away from bulging, sagging, or cracked ceilings.
2. If you see water coming in, put a bucket under it. Do not go on the roof during the storm.
3. Watch for sagging, cracks, or a bowing ceiling. If it bulges or you hear cracking, leave the room and call 911.
4. Keep away from windows and stay inside until the storm passes.

storm over but my heat died n theres ice on the insde of the windows, should we bail to a shelter or wait it out?

Go to a warm shelter now if you can travel safely.
1. Ice inside means your home is losing heat fast. Cold indoors can cause hypothermia.
2. Dress in layers, hat, gloves, and take blankets. Bring medicines and phone charger.
3. Never use a generator, grill, or camp stove indoors. They cause deadly carbon monoxide.
4. If roads are unsafe or you can't leave, call 911. Say you have no heat and ice inside.
5. If you stay, keep one room warm and closed, and check on anyone elderly or sick.

im at school n the ground floor is floodin do we go upstairs or outside w these strangers

Go to a higher floor now. Do not go outside through floodwater.
1. Move upstairs to the highest safe floor. Rising water can trap you on the ground floor.
2. Stay with the group and follow a teacher or staff member. Adults can confirm the plan.
3. Never walk or swim through floodwater. It can hide deep holes, debris, and live wires.
4. Stay away from windows and electrical outlets. Floodwater can carry electric current.
5. Call 911 if someone is hurt or trapped. If water is rising fast, call now.

water comin up the street rn run or stay

Go to high ground now, away from the water.
1. Leave low areas and go uphill or to a tall, solid building's upper floor. Fast water can sweep you away.
2. Do not drive or walk through the water. It can hide deep holes and strong current.
3. Stay away from the shore, river, and street until officials say it is safe.
4. If you cannot reach high ground, go to the highest floor you can and stay there.
5. Call 911 if someone is in danger now.

were near a reactor, what shud we keep in a go bag for radiation?

Get inside and stay put unless officials tell you to leave.
1. Pack a battery or hand-crank radio and spare batteries. You need official instructions when power and phones fail.
2. Add N95 or surgical masks for each person. Masks help stop you breathing in radioactive dust.
3. Add plastic sheeting and duct tape. You can seal windows and doors to keep dust out.
4. Pack bottled water, shelf-stable food, and any medicines. Sealed food and water are safer than exposed supplies.
5. Add a change of clothes and seal dirty clothes in a bag after coming inside. This keeps contamination away from your body.
Do not go outside to evacuate on your own. Leaving into the dust can raise your exposure. Call 911 if someone is injured or in danger.

evac warning for our street do we hav to go rn?

Get ready to leave now. Don't wait to see fire.
1. Check if it's a warning or a mandatory order. An order means go now; a warning means be packed and ready.
2. Pack essentials fast: keys, phone, charger, medicines, ID, water. Keep it light.
3. If there is smoke, fire, or you feel unsafe, leave now. Don't wait for an order.
4. Tell someone where you are going. Call 911 if life is at risk.
5. If you have no car or need help, call 911 now.

my car slid into a drift and the snow keeps comein over the hood, do i stay inside w the engine off

Stay in the car with the engine off. The car is your best shelter.
1. Do not run the engine while snow covers the hood or tailpipe. Buried exhaust can push deadly carbon monoxide inside.
2. If you must run it for heat, first clear snow from the tailpipe and a window. Crack a window open a little.
3. Stay buckled, keep warm with coats and blankets, and move your arms and legs.
4. Make yourself visible: turn on hazard lights and tie something bright to the antenna or window.
5. Call 911 if you are in danger or someone is hurt. Tell them where you are.

car stuck in mud baby hurt pls help

Call 911 now. A hurt baby needs medical help fast.
1. Stay in or near the car unless it is unsafe. Rescuers can find the car more easily than people on foot.
2. Keep the baby warm and still. Do not move the baby more than needed if the neck or back may be hurt.
3. Watch for rising water or ground sliding. If water is rising or the ground is moving, get out and move to higher, solid ground away from the slope.
4. Make yourself easy to see and hear. Turn on hazard lights and honk.

at school w no car if radiation alert comes out how do i leave

Stay inside the school building. Do not leave on foot.
1. Get inside and stay inside. Walls and distance block radiation.
2. Follow school staff and their emergency plan. They know the building and the official instructions.
3. Do not walk or drive out on your own. Roads may be closed and outside air may be contaminated.
4. If told to shelter, close windows and doors and turn off fans or AC. This keeps contaminated air out.
5. Call 911 only if someone is in immediate danger.
Leaving the building during a radiation alert is not safe.

power already flickring shoud i fill bathtub w water b4 ice storm hits

Fill the tub now, before the power goes out.
1. Fill the bathtub and a few clean containers with water. Use tub water for flushing and washing, not drinking.
2. Store drinking water separately in clean jugs. Fill them from the tap now.
3. Keep phones charged. Unplug small appliances and charge power banks while you still have power.
4. Never run a generator, grill, or camp stove indoors or in a garage. Carbon monoxide kills silently.
5. If you use a space heater, keep it 3 feet from anything that can burn and never leave it on while sleeping.
Call 911 if anyone has chest pain, trouble breathing, or confusion.

im at work w my baby and the dirt wall outside the window is moving, i dont speak much english pls tell me where to take her

Move away from that window now.
1. Take your baby and go to the side of the building away from the dirt. Glass and dirt can hit you.
2. If you can get outside safely, walk away from the dirt and go uphill or to flat, solid ground. Do not go downhill. Dirt and mud move fast downhill.
3. Do not go back inside near the dirt. More dirt can fall.
4. Call 911. Say "dirt is moving, landslide." Ask them where to go.
5. Stay away from the dirt wall and any slope until help comes.
